segments.text:
This video will explore
Port Cross References
within Altium Designer.

Adding cross references
to the project

allows us to easily follow
the connective flow of nets

between the schematic sheets
in a project.

The schematic editor supports
automatically creating

and updating
cross references.

First, let's open
all schematics sheets

by right-clicking
on source documents
within the Projects panel

and selecting
Open All Schematic Documents.

Next, let's access
the project options

by right-clicking
on the project

and selecting
Project Options.

The options in the
PCB project window

contain many tabs
along the top.

These will be covered
in further detail in later modules.

However,
here is a quick summary of each.

The Error Reporting tab
within the Project Options dialog

enables us to define
the reporting levels

for each of the
possible electrical
and drafting violations

that can exist on
source schematic documents

when validating
the project.
The Connection Matrix tab

delivers a matrix providing
a mechanism

to establish
connectivity rules

between component pins
and identifiers,

such as ports
and sheet entries.
With the Class Generation tab,

we can configure and control
automatically generated classes

and
user defined classes.
The Comparator tab

enables us to define
which types of differences to find,
and which to ignore,

when comparing
documents.
The ECO Generation tab

enables us to configure
which modification types

can be included when generating
an engineering change order,

based on differences
found by the comparator.
Options.

We will explore this tab
in more detail momentarily.

With the
Multi-Channel tab,

we can define
the room naming scheme

and component
designator format

for use with
multi-channel designs.
The Parameters tab

enables us to manage parameters
defined for the project,

often referred to as
project level parameters.

With the
Device Sheets tab,

we can specify
the folders

in which the device sheets
can be found,
along with their order.

The cross reference settings
exist within the Options tab.

Before we explore
the Cross Reference settings,

let's quickly explore
some of the other sections

of the
Options tab.
Output Path

is the default
output path

for the generation
of output files

from the current
design project.
ECO Log Path

is the default output path
for ECO log files.
Schematic Template Location

is used to specify
a directory

in which to source
schematic template files
for the project.

Within the
Output Options,

we can see
there are four options.
Open outputs after compile

will enable us to
open files

that were generated
after compiling the design project.
Timestamp folder

will enable us
to create a timestamp folder

for the
generated output,

such as
a BOM report.

The folder name will have
a timestamp appended
to the folder name

and will be located in
the output path
specified above.
Archive Project Document

enables us to archive
the project document.
For example,

when generating
manufacturing outputs
from a PCB design.

Use separate folder
for each output type

enables us to create separate folders
for each output type

generated for
the design project.
This folder structure

also will be presented
in the Projects panel.

Now, moving on
to the General area,

we can find the
Automatic Cross References selection.

Check this box to enable
automatic port,
off-sheet connectors,

and sheet entries
cross referencing information

to all source
schematic documents
in the active project.

Within the
Cross Reference section,

there are several options
to discuss.
Sheet Style

provides us options to choose
one of the following sheet styles

for the cross referencing of ports
on a schematic sheet,

or schematic sheets,
within a project.
None.
No sheet style

will be added in the
cross reference string of all ports.

Selecting Name provides
the names of the sheets

that the ports
are linked to

and are added
in the cross reference strings.
Selecting Number

will have the sheet numbers
of the sheets

that the ports
are linked to

added in the
cross reference strings.
Location Style

provides us
options

to choose one of the
following location styles

for the cross referencing
of ports on a schematic sheet,

or schematic sheets,
within a project.
None.

No location style is added
in the cross reference string
of all ports.

Zone refers to the
reference zone numbering,

zones that are often
included in schematic sheet borders

are added in the
cross reference strings of all ports

that are associated
with the parent objects,

such as the location
of sheet symbols.
Location X, Y.

The locations of the ports
are published in brackets

in the cross reference strings
for all ports

that are associated
with the parent objects,

such as the location
of sheet symbols.

When the Follow Cross References
settings in Preferences option
is enabled.

The values of the sheet style
and location style options
will be inherited

from the options in the
Port Cross References region

of the schematic
General page
of the Preferences dialog.
Finally,

moving on to
Display Cross References for,

we have
a few more options.

We can use the
Ports dropdown

to select the mode of displaying
cross references for ports.
Disable.

No cross reference
is added to ports.
Only Related Sheet Entry

will display
the cross reference

to the associated sheet
entry on the parent schematic sheet.

Only Related Ports
displays cross references

to the associated
ports.
Sheet Entry and Ports

displays cross references
to both sheet entries and ports.
Off-sheet Connectors

enables us to display
cross references

for off-sheet
connector objects,
and if desired,

we can also enable
cross references for sheet entries.

Once our cross reference settings
are set,

click OK
on the options dialog.

We can now see the cross references
within our schematic sheets.
If desired,

cross references
can be hidden again

by unchecking the
automatic cross references

within the
Project options dialog.
This concludes our discussion

on port cross references
within Altium Designer.
Thanks for watching.

title: Altium Training - Navigating Schematics: Port Cross References
